checks.title: A database pair or identities fallback exists
checks.proves: The set contains at least one artifact path documented for recovery.
checks.method: Find both participant and validator database evidence, or a structurally recognized identities export.
checks.remediation: Provide the missing participant/validator dump or a validator identities export.
checks.summary: Participant and validator database evidence are present.

checks.title: Identities export has the required offline structure
checks.proves: The export is parseable and contains a participant ID, version, topology snapshot, and required base64 key pairs.
checks.method: Validate JSON types, canonical participant ID prefix, strict base64, and namespace/signing/encryption key names without exposing key bytes.
checks.remediation: Replace the invalid export with a newly captured identities backup; never edit key material by hand.
checks.summary: No identities export is present in this recovery path.

checks.title: Artifact bytes match a capture-time reference
checks.proves: The artifact has not changed since the trusted reference digest was recorded.
checks.method: Compute SHA-256 only for artifacts with a reference digest and compare exact bytes and sizes.
checks.remediation: Replace changed/missing artifacts from trusted storage, or capture and manifest a new complete set.
checks.summary: 2 artifact(s) match capture-time size and SHA-256 references.

checks.title: Validator offset does not exceed participant ledger end
checks.proves: Validator state does not intrinsically reference a Ledger API offset absent from the participant artifact.
checks.method: Compare validator.store_last_ingested_offsets for the latest captured migration with participant.lapi_parameters.ledger_end.
checks.remediation: Discard the inconsistent pair and use a participant backup captured after the validator backup.
checks.summary: Validator offset 3691384 does not exceed participant ledger end 3691388.

checks.title: Latest participant state is inside a sourced sequencer horizon
checks.proves: The captured participant state is not older than the supplied effective catch-up horizon.
checks.method: Compare trusted capture completion time with verification time using a sourced horizon; never infer completion from file mtime.
checks.remediation: Supply capture completion and a versioned documentation-policy or network-operator horizon, or take a new backup.
checks.summary: Backup age 18429s is below the sourced 2592000s sequencer horizon.

checks.title: Selected participant database contains the expected identity
checks.proves: The database selected by the deployment is the database carrying the backup set's expected participant identity.
checks.method: Read identity from the selected restored database and compare it with trusted set or identities-export evidence.
checks.remediation: Supply the effective participant database and expected participant ID, then run crv drill.
checks.summary: The selected restored database contains the expected participant identity.

checks.title: A cross-LSU backup still has a usable synchronizer path
checks.proves: If the backup predates a logical synchronizer upgrade, the captured physical synchronizer is known to remain usable for first restore.
checks.method: Compare captured and current physical synchronizer identity/serial, then evaluate trusted old-synchronizer usability evidence.
checks.remediation: Take a post-LSU backup or supply network-operator evidence that the captured physical synchronizer remains usable.
checks.summary: Captured and current physical synchronizer identity/serial match.
